description:
Two coupled issues:

1. `Interactive.handle_event` catchall clause at line 86
   swallows the `:cancel` event that `Components.Input` returns
   when Escape is pressed. Escape currently does nothing.

2. `Components.Input.handle_key/2` covers enter/left/right/
   home/end/backspace/delete but is missing the full set of
   upstream `input.test.ts` scenarios (port-map §14.1, 580
   lines): kill ring semantics (save/delete cycle for Ctrl+W/
   U/K/Alt+D, Alt+Y yank-pop both directions), undo/redo with
   coalescing, wide-char cursor tracking, horizontal scroll on
   narrow widths.

Scope:
- `handle_event({:key, %Key{key: :escape}})` in Interactive:
  clear the input field. Double-Escape exits (matches upstream
  double-Ctrl+C pattern, different key for muscle memory).
- Input.handle_key/2 gains all the editing ops from upstream
  (kill ring + undo). `insert/2` grows paste handling.
- Port the upstream input.test.ts scenarios verbatim — match
  intent and quality of the 580 lines of cases.

TDD:
- Every case from input.test.ts mirrored
- Escape clears input; double-Escape exits
- Kill ring: Ctrl+W deletes word, Ctrl+Y yanks, Alt+Y cycles
- Undo: coalesces consecutive chars, splits on spaces,
  preserves across cursor moves
title: Escape key handling + Input.handle_key upstream parity
